findings.title: Imported feed HTML bypasses Discourse sanitization
findings.body: Imported content is stored with `cook_method: raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns that raw value without running the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `PollFeed` passes arbitrary RSS/Atom item content directly into this method, so a feed containing `<script>`, event-handler attributes, or dangerous URLs can persist executable HTML. The embed view then renders `post.cooked` with `raw`, making this stored XSS execute for visitors of the embedding site (and the imported post may also be exposed through normal topic views). Sanitize imported HTML with the same allowlist used for posts before storing/rendering it, rather than using raw HTML as a sanitizer bypass.

findings.title: Concurrent imports of the same URL can fail on the unique index
findings.body: The code performs a non-locking lookup and then creates the `TopicEmbed`; two retrieve jobs for the same URL can both see no row and both create posts before one loses on the unique `embed_url` index. The losing transaction raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and the job fails instead of returning the already-created embed. This is especially reachable because staff requests bypass throttling and scheduled feed polling can overlap retrieval. Handle the unique-conflict case (or use a locking/upsert strategy) and return/reload the winning embed.

findings.title: Relative links without a leading slash are not converted to source URLs
findings.body: `absolutize_urls` claims to convert relative URLs, but it only rewrites values beginning with `/`. Valid relative values such as `images/photo.jpg`, `../next.html`, and `page.html` remain relative in the stored raw HTML. When rendered by Discourse, browsers resolve them relative to the Discourse embed page rather than the source article, causing imported links and images to point to nonexistent or unintended local Discourse paths. Resolve all non-absolute HTTP(S) URLs against the source URI, while preserving fragment/mailto/etc. behavior as appropriate.

findings.title: postMessage origin validation accepts unrelated origins that are URL substrings
findings.body: The receiver treats an origin as trusted when it appears anywhere in `discourseUrl`. For example, if the forum URL is `https://forum.example.com/`, the distinct origin `https://forum.example.co` passes this check because it is a prefix substring. A page on such an origin can send `discourse-resize` messages and control the iframe height. Parse `discourseUrl` and compare `e.origin` for exact origin equality instead of using substring matching.
